blocks.md:
- A projectile is a particle moving freely, under gravity, in a two-dimensional plane
- Examples of projectile motion include ![2-6-1-horizontal-_-vertical-components-diagram-1](assets/1bd8ea85b196-2-6-1-horizontal-vertical-components-diagram-1.png)

  - Sports such as basketball, javelin, archery, etc
  - Computer games such as Angry Birds

- The modelling assumptions with projectiles are

  - **No air resistance**, no horizontal forces
  - The projectile **moves freely** under gravity (no other vertical forces)
  - **Ignore spin** and the **rotation** of the projectile
  - Motion is **symmetrical** along the path of a **parabola**

blocks.text: What is the acceleration of a projectile?

blocks.md:
- As it is 2D there will be a horizontal component to acceleration (**a**<sub>**x**</sub>) and a vertical component (**a**<sub>**y**</sub>)
- There will be **no** horizontal acceleration (**a**<sub>**x**</sub>** = 0**)

  - No forces are acting horizontally
  - **Horizontal speed** is **constant**
- There will be constant vertical acceleration (due to gravity, **a**<sub>**y**</sub>** = ± g**)
- **a**<sub>**y**</sub> may be positive or negative depending on which direction is taken as positive
- The acceleration can be written as 2D vector

blocks.text: What is the initial velocity of a projectile?

blocks.md:
- As it is 2D there will be a horizontal component to the **initial velocity**(**u**<sub>**x**</sub>**)** and a vertical component (**u**<sub>**y**</sub>)
- A projectile is launched with **initial speed** *U* m s<sup>-1</sup> at an angle θ to the horizontal

  - If it is projected **below** the horizontal then θ would be **negative**
- Its initial velocity, **u** m s<sup>-1</sup>, is a vector with:

  - horizontal component, **u**<sub>**x**</sub> = *U* cosθ
  - vertical component, **u**<sub>**y**</sub> = *U* sinθ
- The initial velocity can have a **positive** or **negative vertical component** as an object can be projected **upwards** or **downwards**

blocks.label: Worked Example
blocks.md:
A projectile is launched at an angle of 25° to the horizontal with speed 5 m s<sup>-1</sup> .

Find the initial velocity, **u** m s<sup>-1</sup> , of the projectile.

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
- Sometimes they may give you the initial velocity as a vector already. To find the initial speed you would find the magnitude of the initial velocity and to find the angle of projection you could sketch a diagram and use trigonometry.
- The horizontal speed is always constant so there will never be a point during the motion when the speed of the object is zero. Its minimum speed will be at its maximum height when its vertical velocity is instantaneously zero.
